rows.grounds: instrumental plural of ānanda, indicating the means
vocative address to the supreme goddess
genitive plural of bhakta, denoting those who receive benefit
compound of hita (welfare) and kāriṇī (doing, causing), describing the goddess

items.question: Through what means does the supreme goddess accomplish the welfare of devotees?
premises: The supreme goddess is directly addressed.
Devotees are the recipients of her beneficial action.
Blisses function as the means of her benefaction.
items.inference: The supreme goddess accomplishes the welfare of devotees through blisses.
uncertainties: The specific nature of the blisses (ānandaiḥ) is not further specified in this verse.
items.plain_english: O supreme goddess, you bring welfare to the devotees through blisses.
